subject: DPA scope clarifications and signature routing - Horizon Health
messages:
From: Danielle Cruz <danielle.cruz@horizonhealth.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@horizonhealth.com, m.thompson@horizonhealth.com
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Horizon DPA - redlines and retention questions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. Attached are our redlines to Redwood's standard DPA (Horizon_DPA_v1_redlines.docx). There are a few items we need clarified before legal can sign:

- Data retention: Section 4.2 lists 90 days for logs; can you confirm whether that includes aggregated WL logs we request for debugging? We prefer 180 days for those.
- Subprocessors: We need the current subprocessor list for US-hosted instances and an approval workflow for adding new subprocessors.
- SCCs + international transfers: We need confirmation that Redwood will execute SCCs for EU-derived data and whether you maintain a DPA variant with SCCs embedded.

We'd like to keep momentum on the procurement timeline. Can you please route to your legal and share a proposed counter or an explicit yes/no on the three points above? If you prefer, we can do a quick 30-min call with Markus (legal) and Lauren (procurement) on your side.

Best,
Danielle
Danielle Cruz
Sr. Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Horizon Health
Attachments: Horizon_DPA_v1_redlines.docx (document, 42KB)

From: rachel.kim@redwood.com
To: Danielle Cruz <danielle.cruz@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-05T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Horizon DPA - redlines and retention questions

Hi Danielle — thanks for the redlines and clear list. Looping in Markus (Legal) and Lauren (Sales Ops) to triage. Quick answers up front so your team can plan:

- Retention: Our standard logging retention is 90 days for raw request/response logs; aggregated/telemetry logs are 180 days. We can extend specific debug logs to 180 days by exception for Horizon; that would be documented in the DPA annex.
- Subprocessors: We'll share the current US subprocessor registry (S3, Datadog, Cloud provider DB). For add/remove workflow, Redwood uses a 14-day notification window and an approval escalation for exceptions; Markus will confirm language.
- SCCs: Redwood can execute SCCs. We maintain a DPA variant with SCCs embedded for EU transfers; that would be appended if EU personal data are in scope.

Markus — can you propose narrow counter-language for the retention clause and confirm subprocessors + approval workflow? Lauren — can you summarize expected procurement timeline so we can align signature routing and DocuSign envelope?

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0134

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com, Danielle Cruz <danielle.cruz@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-05T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Horizon DPA - redlines and retention questions

Hi all,

Thanks for the clear redlines. I reviewed the doc and propose the following narrow counterpoints to keep the deal moving:

1) Logs/Retention (Section 4.2) — counter: Redwood will retain raw request/response logs for 90 days and aggregated telemetry for 180 days. For debug traces that contain PII, Redwood will retain up to 180 days on a per-request basis if Horizon provides a written exception request tied to a support ticket. We'll add an annex that lists allowable debug categories and the exception process.

2) Subprocessors — counter: Redwood will provide the current subprocessor list within 3 business days and will notify customers of material additions 14 days prior to onboarding. For any data-critical subprocessors (as defined in Annex A), Redwood will obtain written consent; for others, notice-only. We can include a schedule that flags US production vs backup-only providers.

3) SCCs and transfers — counter: Redwood will execute the European Commission SCCs (2021 module) and can append the SCCs to the DPA if EU personal data are in scope. We will also include a short-MFA (security) attestation summary in the annex.

I attached a one-page counter DPA (Redwood_DPA_counter_v1.docx) with redlines for the three bullets above. If Horizon is comfortable with the annex approach for debug retention and the subprocessor schedule, we can prepare a DocuSign envelope and request signature from the Horizon legal signatory.

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_counter_v1.docx (docx, 18KB)

From: Danielle Cruz <danielle.cruz@horizonhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Horizon DPA - redlines and retention questions

Markus / Rachel — thanks for the quick turnaround and the annex approach. A few clarifications from our side:

- The exception workflow for debug traces looks acceptable; please add the ticketing SLA (we prefer 5 business days for acknowledgement).
- For subprocessors: please mark the cloud backup provider as backup-only in the schedule; we will want written notice and the opportunity to object for primary data processors only.
- SCCs: please append SCCs and send the DPA variant with SCCs embedded; Horizon needs that before signing.

If you can update the counter-doc with these three clarifications, we can run it through our legal intake and target signature by 2026-12-10. Also please include a short cover email with routing so procurement knows who signs on Redwood's side.

Danielle

On the signature routing, procurement will expect a DocuSign envelope addressed to Michael Thompson (legal signatory) and cc: procurement@horizonhealth.com.

Danielle Cruz

Horizon Health
